newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh Bengal Biscuits may offer bonus.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh Bengal Biscuits may offer bonus.

text.p: Bangladesh's Bengal Biscuits Limited is unlikely to pay any dividend for year 1996, which ended on June 30, but may offer a one-for-five bonus share, company officials said on Wednesday.

The company is not paying any cash dividend for the year to finance its expansion programme. "We are not in a position to pay any dividend because we need a huge amount of capital for our two expansion projects," said General Manager M.H. Dhali.
The annual general meeting is set for Friday. The company paid a 20 percent dividend on its 100-taka share in the previous year.
The officials said the expansion would cost nearly 70 million taka.
In 1995/96, sales rose by 36.54 percent to more than 230 million taka from 170 million taka the previous year.
"As a result, the net profit will rise by 79.59 percent to more than 30 million taka from 16.8 million taka during 1994/95," M.A. Kalam, chairman of the company, told Reuters.
